title: Google AI Edge Gallery - Local Gemma 4 Models on iPhone
description: Google released an official app for running Gemma 4 models (E2B and E4B sizes) directly on iPhone. The app works remarkably well with the 2.54GB E2B model being both fast and useful. Features include image Q&A, audio transcription (up to 30s), and 'skills' demo showing tool calling against eight interactive widgets (interactive-map, kitchen-adventure, calculate-hash, text-spinner, mood-tracker, mnemonic-password, query-wikipedia, qr-code). First time a local model vendor released an official iPhone app, though it's missing permanent conversation logs.
author: Simon Willison

title: datasette-ports 0.2 Released
description: Release of datasette-ports 0.2 - a tool to find all currently running Datasette instances and list their ports. No longer requires Datasette - running 'uvx datasette-ports' now works standalone. Installing as a Datasette plugin continues to provide the 'datasette ports' command.
author: Simon Willison

title: OpenAI Alums Launch $100M Investment Fund
description: OpenAI alumni have been quietly investing from a new potentially $100M fund, showing continued financial activity in the AI space from former OpenAI personnel.
author: TechCrunch

title: Google Quietly Launches Offline-First AI Dictation App on iOS
description: Google quietly released an AI dictation app that works offline on iOS, similar to the AI Edge Gallery app for running local models.
author: TechCrunch

title: Iran Threatens 'Stargate' AI Data Centers
description: Geopolitical tensions involving AI infrastructure as Iran threatens 'Stargate' AI data centers, highlighting the strategic importance of AI computing facilities.
author: TechCrunch

title: Eight Years of Wanting, Three Months of Building with AI - SyntaQLite
description: Lalit Maganti's long-form piece on agentic engineering: spent 8 years thinking about and 3 months building syntaqlite (high-fidelity devtools for SQLite with parser, formatter, and verifier). The key insight: AI excels at tedious work like 400+ grammar rules. Claude Code helped build the first prototype, but they eventually threw it away and started from scratch - AI made them procrastinate on key design decisions because refactoring felt cheap. Important lesson about AI-assisted development: great for low-level details and prototyping, but can lead to deferred architectural decisions that corrode clear thinking.
author: Simon Willison (citing Lalit Maganti)

title: Japan Proving Experimental Physical AI Ready for Real World
description: In Japan, robots aren't coming for jobs - they're filling jobs nobody wants. Shows practical deployment of physical AI in real-world scenarios.
author: TechCrunch

title: Copilot 'For Entertainment Purposes Only' Per Microsoft Terms
description: Microsoft's terms of service indicate Copilot is 'for entertainment purposes only', raising questions about liability and production use guarantees for AI coding assistants.
author: TechCrunch

title: GitHub Activity Surging: 275 Million Commits Per Week
description: GitHub platform activity is accelerating dramatically. There were 1 billion commits in 2025. Now it's 275 million commits per week, on pace for 14 billion this year if growth remains linear. GitHub Actions grew from 500M minutes/week in 2023 to 1B minutes/week in 2025, and now 2.1B minutes so far this week (2026). Shows massive explosion in development activity, likely driven by AI coding tools.
author: Simon Willison (citing Kyle Daigle, GitHub COO)

title: Anthropic Says Claude Code Subscribers Need Extra Payment for OpenClaw
description: Anthropic announced that Claude Code subscribers will need to pay extra for OpenClaw usage, introducing new pricing tiers for advanced coding features.
author: TechCrunch

title: OpenAI Executive Shuffle: New Roles for COO Brad Lightcap
description: OpenAI executive shuffle includes new role for COO Brad Lightcap to lead 'special projects', along with new roles for Fidji Simo and Kate Rouch.
author: TechCrunch

title: Anthropic Buys Biotech Startup Coefficient Bio in $400M Deal
description: Anthropic acquires biotech startup Coefficient Bio in a $400M deal, expanding into AI applications for biotechnology research.
author: TechCrunch

title: AI Companies Building Huge Natural Gas Plants for Data Centers
description: AI companies are constructing massive natural gas power plants to support energy-intensive data centers, raising environmental and infrastructure concerns.
author: TechCrunch

title: Vulnerability Research Is Cooked - AI Agents Finding Zero Days
description: Thomas Ptacek's analysis of how frontier models are drastically altering vulnerability research and exploit development. Within months, coding agents will handle most high-impact vulnerability research by pointing an agent at source code. Agents excel at this because LLMs encode: (1) supernatural amounts of correlation across vast codebases, (2) complete library of documented bug classes, (3) pattern matching and constraint solving abilities, (4) ability to search forever without boredom. Vulnerability research is 'the perfect problem for an LLM agent' - outcomes are testable success/failure trials.
author: Simon Willison (citing Thomas Ptacek)

title: Anthropic Ramps Up Political Activities with New PAC

title: OpenAI Acquires TBPN Business Talk Show

title: Highlights from Lenny's Podcast on Agentic Engineering
description: Simon Willison was a guest on Lenny Rachitsky's podcast discussing 'An AI state of the union: We've passed the inflection point, dark factories are coming, and automation timelines'. Episode covers agentic engineering, coding agents, and the current state of AI development. Available on YouTube, Spotify, and Apple Podcasts.
author: Simon Willison

title: datasette-llm 0.1a6 Released
description: Release of datasette-llm 0.1a6, an LLM integration plugin for Datasette that other plugins can depend on. Part of Simon's ongoing work building LLM tooling.
author: Simon Willison

title: Agentic-MME: What Agentic Capability Really Brings to Multimodal Intelligence?
description: ArXiv paper exploring what agentic capabilities truly bring to multimodal intelligence systems. Investigates the unique advantages of agentic AI architectures in handling complex multimodal tasks.
author: Qianshan Wei et al.

title: AgentHazard: Benchmark for Evaluating Harmful Behavior in Computer-Use Agents
description: ArXiv paper introducing AgentHazard, a benchmark designed to evaluate harmful behaviors in computer-using AI agents. Important for AI safety research as agents gain more autonomy.
author: Yunhao Feng et al.

title: Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning for Tool-Calling Agents
description: ArXiv paper on multi-turn reinforcement learning approaches for tool-calling agents with iterative reward calibration. Addresses challenges in training agents that effectively use external tools.
author: Wachiravit Modecrua et al.

title: FoE: Forest of Errors Makes First Solution Best in Large Reasoning Models
description: ArXiv paper presenting FoE (Forest of Errors), a technique to make the first solution the best in large reasoning models through error-based tree approaches.
author: Kehan Jiang et al.

title: InfoSeeker: Scalable Hierarchical Parallel Agent Framework for Web Information Seeking
description: ArXiv paper introducing InfoSeeker, a hierarchical parallel agent framework designed for efficient web information seeking. Addresses scalability in multi-agent web research systems.
author: Ka Yiu Lee et al.

title: Automatic Textbook Formalization
description: ArXiv paper on automatic formalization of textbooks, using AI to convert educational content into formal mathematical representations. Important for AI education and verification.
author: Fabian Gloeckle et al.

title: SCRAT: Coupled Control, Structured Memory, and Verifiable Action in Agentic AI
description: ArXiv paper presenting SCRAT (Stochastic Control with Retrieval and Auditable Trajectories), drawing insights from squirrel locomotion and scatter-hoarding for agentic AI architectures with verifiable actions.
author: Maximiliano Armesto, Christophe Kolb
